script: Respect time off and don't 'stress' you on your days off? Sure. Works both ways.. I don't work for the best company—it's corporate and the higher ups have little understanding of what goes on at ground level. When I started, I had a manager who actually protected us from the usual crap that rolls down the hill. He was promoted out of the store, and after a few misfires we got a new manager. She's loud, swears like a sailor, and drops controversial opinions in conversations with friends. Customers quietly ask why I didn't report her, then roll their eyes when I say, "She IS my manager." I thought it was over. It wasn't. There's a system for who to call when no manager is available. We're a tiny team, most of us solo. If the manager is coming in the morning, we call her the night before with concerns. If she's not there, we call the assistant. Sure, no problem. But here's the thing… I found an issue that felt like a health code violation from one of our vendors. I took pictures, shot a short text explaining it, and sent it right away instead of waiting until she worked. The exact text I sent: "I need you guys to understand that if the store is not on fire, your not being robbed your need to be contacting (assistant managers name) not me unless its an emergency please." Four days later she texts me scolding me for "not doing my job" when it was a managerial level job, not mine. A few minutes later, she says "oh, you DID do it. sorry" and drops a list of points in our store's "good job" system. I didn't respond because I wasn't on the clock. If this didn't work, I'd lose everything. I felt the sting. She then texts, asking what my pay rate was for her review. I decided to answer—after all, it's her job to know. She started texting me random stuff: "do you know where the scissors went?" and other non‑emergency questions. According to the precedent she set, it was not a store emergency and not my problem until I was on the clock. I decided that I will not answer her if I am not on the clock. She calls, I let it go to voicemail. She texts, I leave her on read until I am on the clock. Now the company has a "no phones while on the clock" policy. She can't text or call me while I am on the clock unless she uses the store phone. That's a whole other can of worms— they want us to use a mandatory app for store communication but not have our phones out. I asked for clarification on the welcome message on the new app, asking if they're lifting the phones at work ban or expect us to work off the clock. Everyone in the company saw my question, and the answer was "we'll get back to you," which hasn't happened. Now nobody is using the app because the policy says we can't laugh out loud. But wait— it gets worse. She will have to come in, in person, on her days off if she wants to talk to me. Maybe she should not have chewed my ass out so hard when I just sent her one text. I was about to hit send when my phone buzzed again…
